payload.report: The patient's refractory tension-like headaches are explained by a benign/inflammatory nasopharyngeal lesion rather than neoplasm or primary headache. Bilateral nasopharyngeal fullness, MRI restricted diffusion, endoscopic purulence from an enlarged cystic torus tubarius, benign reactive pathology, and growth of S. lugdunensis converge. Pathology, the gold standard, excludes neoplasm; all specialists agree on an infectious/inflammatory cause. The most specific supported hypothesis is S. lugdunensis infectious/inflammatory nasopharyngeal lesion (0.9). An infected cyst/abscess variant (0.6) remains plausible but unconfirmed by cyst wall/abscess pathology or follow-up imaging. Thus the diagnosis is S. lugdunensis nasopharyngitis.
